client.name: Adrian Tan
client.background: Adrian Tan is a business owner who manages his personal investments separately from his company's operating finances. He prefers deliberate portfolio decisions and keeps organised records, often asking for explanations in plain language before proceeding.
client.investment_objective: Reduce exposure to global equity market volatility and make funds available for anticipated personal expenditure while retaining a measured approach to his remaining investments.
client.loss_attitude: Adrian accepts that market investments can incur losses and is willing to realise a loss when reducing exposure serves his needs. He dislikes rushed decisions and wants to understand the trade-off between waiting for a preferred price and completing a sale.

setting.call_reason: Adrian has arranged a telephone review of his existing Summit Global Equity ETF holding because his personal spending plans and preference for lower market exposure have changed. The call centres on a considered reduction of the holding through a limit sale.
setting.conversation_style: An extended, courteous private-banking conversation in natural Singapore English. Adrian is methodical and asks follow-up questions about market behaviour, price control and execution uncertainty. Melissa uses accessible explanations, allows space for reflection and keeps the discussion focused while accommodating occasional neutral small talk.

final_product.description: Summit Global Equity ETF is an exchange-traded fund providing exposure to a diversified portfolio of global equities. Its exchange-traded structure allows the client to seek a sale at a specified minimum price, but execution depends on available buyers and market conditions.
concrete_risks: The ETF's market value can decline when global equity markets fall, including during periods of correlated selling across regions.
The ETF's traded price can differ from the value of its underlying holdings, particularly during market stress.
Reduced trading liquidity or wider bid-ask spreads can make it harder to sell at the client's preferred price.
A sell limit order may remain unexecuted if buyers do not meet the specified limit, leaving the client exposed to subsequent market movements.
final_product.recommendation_basis: Reducing the existing Summit Global Equity ETF holding supports Adrian's objective of lowering equity-market exposure and releasing funds for personal expenditure. A limit order also accommodates his preference for controlling the minimum acceptable sale price, with the trade-off that the sale may not complete.

scenario.holding_context: Adrian already holds Summit Global Equity ETF in his personal investment portfolio and wishes to reduce that existing position rather than add exposure.
additional_discussion_topics: The client's changing work routine and plans to delegate more operational responsibilities
Family preferences for quieter holidays and time together
The client's experience using the bank's online interface
Gardening and finding time for outdoor activities
